solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: ! Kinky games are not restricting one in relationship

indicators.note: restricting means hemming in, so the rearranged letters close around the numeral
kinky means twisted or bent, so the letters of these three words are twisted into a new order

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A warning that saucy bedroom games are off limits for one person in a couple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kinky' rearranges GAMES ARE NOT, and 'restricting' puts I (one) inside that jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase names a household or sexual arrangement involving three people, so it is a kind of relationship.

clue.text: One delivers in French south going about with iron

indicators.note: going about means surrounding, so the French south is put around the abbreviation

parts.note: le Midi is the south of France
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

explanation.surface: Someone making deliveries in the south of France, carrying an iron.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One delivers' sounds like a courier, but it is a person who delivers babies; 'in' only links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A midwife's job is to deliver babies, so she is someone who delivers.

clue.text: Veto taking over year to satisfy one abroad

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means turned up, so the run of pieces is read from the bottom upward

parts.note: to fill a need is to satisfy it
un is French for one, so it is one in a foreign tongue

explanation.surface: A veto being used for a year to please a foreigner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Over' reverses the whole string of three pieces, not just the year; 'taking' only links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To veto something is to cancel or annul its effect, which is what the verb means.

clue.text: Weed reduced to powder smells occasionally

parts.note: something reduced to powder has been ground

indicators.note: occasionally means only now and then, so every other letter of smells is used

parts.note: the first, third and fifth letters of smells

explanation.surface: A weed that has been pulverised gives off a faint smell now and then.
explanation.definitionFit: Groundsel is a common yellow-flowered plant of the daisy family that gardeners treat as a weed.

clue.text: Valuable sort perhaps Texan behind film

parts.note: ass is the American word for the backside, so a Texan, as an example of an American, might call his behind this
E.T. is the Spielberg film

explanation.surface: A rich Texan with a film career looks like a valuable person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Behind' is not a position here: it is the noun, the bottom, in American English.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who is very useful to a team or firm is called an asset to it.

clue.text: Explorer, fairly short, drinking beer

indicators.note: drinking means taking in, so the shortened word goes around the beer
short means cut off at the end, so the last letter goes

parts.note: to treat someone right is to treat them fairly, justly
ale is a type of beer

explanation.surface: An explorer, a fairly short man, has a drink of beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fairly short' looks like a description of the explorer's height, but 'short' acts on the word for 'fairly'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Walter Raleigh was the Elizabethan adventurer who led expeditions to the Americas.

clue.text: Sound from egg on penetration

indicators.note: sound from means what is heard when a word is said, so the answer is spoken like a synonym for egg on

parts.note: to egg someone on is to incite them

explanation.surface: The noise an egg makes as it is pierced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Egg on' reads as a breakfast topping but is the verb meaning urge.
explanation.definitionFit: Penetration can mean keen understanding, the ability to see deeply into something, which is insight.

clue.text: See wriggly insect served up in comfort food

indicators.note: in means placed within, so the other pieces go inside the word for comfort

parts.note: to cheer someone is to comfort them

indicators.note: wriggly means squirming, so the letters of see are shuffled
in a down clue, served up means brought upward, so the insect is read backwards

parts.note: a grub is an insect larva

explanation.surface: Look: a wriggling bug turns up in someone's favourite comfort dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Comfort food' looks like one phrase, but only 'food' is the definition; 'comfort' is a verb meaning to console.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheeseburger is a fast-food sandwich of a beef patty topped with cheese in a bun.

clue.text: Happy to return ring on greeting nobleman

indicators.note: on means placed after, so the reversed word and the ring follow the greeting

parts.note: hi is a greeting

indicators.note: to return means to go back, so happy is written backwards

parts.note: glad means happy
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: Someone glad to get the ring back after greeting a nobleman.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'on' means placed after, so the greeting comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: A hidalgo is a member of the lower nobility in Spain, a minor nobleman.

clue.text: Fabric close to crease in sail is coming apart

indicators.note: in means placed within, so the letter goes inside the rearranged words
coming apart means falling to pieces, so the letters of sail is are broken up and rearranged
close to means the end of, so the last letter of crease is taken

parts.note: the last letter of crease

explanation.surface: A sail made of some fabric is splitting along a crease.
explanation.walkthrough: E, from the end of 'crease', goes inside a rearrangement of SAIL IS. 'Fabric' looks like sailcloth, but the answer is also a historical region.
explanation.definitionFit: Silesia is a twilled cotton cloth used for linings, named after the region where it was made.

clue.text: A member ran into criticism about arena

parts.note: MP stands for Member of Parliament
to run into something is to hit it
heat can mean strong criticism or pressure
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: An MP has run into a storm of criticism concerning a stadium.
explanation.definitionFit: An amphitheatre is a round open-air venue with tiered seating around a central space, an arena.

clue.text: Volume in electronic speech, not constant

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for electronic, as in e-mail

indicators.note: not means without, so the letter for the constant is dropped

parts.note: diction is a manner of speech or enunciation
c is the symbol for a constant in maths and for the speed of light

explanation.surface: Turning the volume up and down in electronic speech that keeps varying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not constant' reads as 'varying' but tells you to remove the letter that stands for a constant; 'Volume' is a book, not loudness.
explanation.definitionFit: An edition is a published version of a book, and a volume is one book in a set.

clue.text: Scots one flourishing at last in ram tethering

indicators.note: in means inside, so the other pieces are placed within the ram

parts.note: a tup is a ram
yin is the Scots word for one

indicators.note: at last means the final letter of flourishing

parts.note: the last letter of flourishing

explanation.surface: A Scot with a thriving flock finally tying up a ram.
explanation.walkthrough: Tup is a British dialect word for a ram, and yin is Scots for one.
explanation.definitionFit: Tethering an animal means fastening it with a rope, which is tying it up.

clue.text: Sombre song for one gaining entry to cathedral city

indicators.note: gaining entry to means getting inside, so the abbreviation goes into the city

parts.note: Ely in Cambridgeshire is a small city famous for its cathedral
e.g. means for example, for one

explanation.surface: A mournful hymn admitted to services in a cathedral town.
explanation.walkthrough: Ely is a small English cathedral city in the Fens.
explanation.definitionFit: An elegy is a mournful poem or piece of music, often a lament for the dead.

clue.text: Get hollow pasta? This is different?

definitions.text: Get hollow pasta? This is different?

indicators.note: different means changed, so these letters are rearranged into a new word
hollow means emptied of its inside, so only the outer letters of pasta remain

parts.note: the first and last letters of pasta

explanation.surface: Someone wondering whether to buy hollow pasta like macaroni, and whether this long thin kind is not the same.
explanation.walkthrough: GET, PA (hollowed 'pasta') and THIS together are rearranged. The whole clue also points to the answer, since spaghetti is a solid pasta, unlike hollow kinds such as macaroni.
explanation.definitionFit: Spaghetti is long, thin, solid pasta, so it is unlike hollow kinds such as penne or macaroni.

clue.text: Bible book detailed in a movement that's tasteful

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the shortened book goes within the other two pieces

parts.note: a tic is an involuntary twitching movement

indicators.note: detailed means with the tail cut off, so the last letter goes

parts.note: Esther is a book of the Old Testament

explanation.surface: A book of the Bible is explained in detail as part of a tasteful artistic movement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Detailed' looks like 'in detail' but means de-tailed: the book loses its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Something aesthetic is pleasing in appearance and shows good taste.

clue.text: Countries together resolve southern troubles

parts.note: the UN, the United Nations, is countries acting together
to settle a dispute is to resolve it

explanation.surface: Nations acting together to sort out problems in the south.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Troubles' looks like a noun but is the verb, as in 'it troubles me'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that unsettles a person disturbs or worries them, so it troubles them.

clue.text: Resilience enlivens European taken out in recession

indicators.note: in recession means going backwards, so the shortened word is reversed
taken out means removed, so the letter for European is dropped

parts.note: to animate something is to enliven it

explanation.surface: An economy's resilience livens up Europe after it is removed from a recession.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping E from ANIMATES gives ANIMATS, which 'in recession' reverses.
explanation.definitionFit: Stamina is staying power, the ability to keep going and recover, which is a form of resilience.

clue.text: Craft perfectly capturing upper-class country

indicators.note: capturing means holding inside, so the phrase goes around the other two pieces

parts.note: to a T means perfectly
U stands for upper-class, as in U and non-U
GB stands for Great Britain

explanation.surface: A boat that perfectly captures the upper-class country.
explanation.walkthrough: TO A T splits around U and GB.
explanation.definitionFit: A tugboat is a small powerful vessel that tows ships, and craft is a general word for boats.

clue.text: Scarcity will have 500 leaving planet

indicators.note: leaving means going away, so the Roman numeral is removed

parts.note: a dearth is a scarcity or shortage
D is the Roman numeral for 500

explanation.surface: A shortage will mean five hundred people leaving the planet.
explanation.definitionFit: Earth is the third world from the sun, the one we live on.

clue.text: Having lost identity Coleridge violated painter

indicators.note: violated means abused or broken, so the remaining letters are rearranged
having lost means being without, so the letters for identity are taken away

parts.note: ID is short for identity, as on an ID card

explanation.surface: The poet Coleridge, robbed of his identity, was assaulted by a painter.
explanation.walkthrough: Without ID, COLERIDGE leaves COLERGE, and 'violated' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: El Greco was the Cretan-born artist who worked in Spain, known for elongated religious figures.

clue.text: Comes round to upping prices externally

indicators.note: externally means on the outside, so the word for prices goes around the other piece

parts.note: rates are prices or charges

indicators.note: in a down clue, upping means turning upwards, so the word is reversed

explanation.surface: Someone comes round to the idea of raising prices on outside trade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upping prices' looks like a price rise, but 'upping' belongs to 'to' and reverses it in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that rotates turns about an axis, so it comes round again and again.

clue.text: Maybe neon light moving left across city

indicators.note: moving means changing place, so the letter for left travels to a new spot
across means to the other side, so the letter moves over the gas to sit just after its first letter

parts.note: neon is an example of a gas
glow means light

explanation.surface: A neon sign's light is moving leftwards across a city skyline.
explanation.walkthrough: GAS + GLOW gives GASGLOW; the L moves across the A and S of GAS to give GLASGOW. 'Left' is not a direction here but the letter L.
explanation.definitionFit: Glasgow is the largest city in Scotland, on the River Clyde.

clue.text: Rugby team is no more, I should add

parts.note: was is the past tense, describing what is no more
PS, postscript, is what a writer adds at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: A rugby team has folded, the writer adds as an afterthought.
explanation.walkthrough: Wasps is an English rugby union club, which did go out of business in 2022.
explanation.definitionFit: Wasps is the name of a professional English rugby union side.

clue.text: Leaves drink after wasted meal

indicators.note: after means following, so the drink comes behind the word for wasted

parts.note: wasted is slang for drunk or stoned, so high
tea is a drink made from leaves

explanation.surface: Someone heads off for a drink after a wasted meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' looks like a verb, someone departing, but is the noun: tea leaves. High tea is a British early-evening meal with a cooked dish, bread and tea.
explanation.definitionFit: High tea is a substantial early-evening meal eaten with tea, especially in northern Britain.

clue.text: What might suggest our US causing destruction?

parts.note: these words are not a definition but the result: splitting the answer into a short abbreviation, a containment word and a word of three letters gives an instruction whose letters spell our US

explanation.surface: Something that could hint at the destruction of America.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a reverse clue: the answer split as RU IN OUS is a recipe, and following it gives the letters of 'our US'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruinous means bringing ruin or disaster, so wrecking or destroying.

clue.text: Speaker pretty terse before start of session

parts.note: twee means overly pretty or quaint

indicators.note: before start of session means only the part of terse coming before the letter S, the first letter of session, is kept

explanation.surface: A speaker who is pretty curt just before a meeting begins.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the part of 'terse' that comes before its S, the start of 'session', is kept; 'Speaker' is a loudspeaker, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: A tweeter is a small loudspeaker that reproduces high-frequency sounds.

clue.text: Crusader emblem in sweet old ship rounding cape

indicators.note: rounding means going around, so the other pieces enclose the letter for cape

parts.note: a Malteser is a chocolate-covered malt ball, a British sweet
C is the map abbreviation for cape
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: A crusader's badge on an old sweet ship sailing round a headland.
explanation.walkthrough: Maltesers are British chocolate-covered malt balls; the cape letter sits just before the sweet's final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The eight-pointed cross was the emblem of the Knights Hospitaller, the crusading order later based on Malta.
